title: Immunotherapy resistance in NSCLC
summary: Explore why responses to immune-checkpoint therapies differ, and how public cohorts can support careful, reproducible comparisons.
question: Which pretreatment tumour and immune features have reproducible associations with response to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade?
approach: Define response endpoints and baseline characteristics before comparing cohorts.
Inspect GEO expression datasets alongside clinical annotations; check assay compatibility.
Search primary studies for both supporting and contradictory evidence.
Report confidence intervals, limitations and differences between association and causation.
cautions: Small, heterogeneous public cohorts cannot establish a clinically reliable predictor of treatment response. This card does not present a treatment recommendation.

title: The tumour microenvironment
summary: Investigate how interacting cells, extracellular signals and tissue context shape how cancer behaves.
question: What cellular and immune features can be measured consistently across tumour tissue studies?
approach: Separate different cell types and measurement approaches.
Distinguish tissue observations from computational cell-mixture estimates.
Compare findings across cancer types only with clear context.
cautions: Concept imagery on this card is not a pathology scan or experimental finding.

title: Antigen presentation and immune recognition
summary: Trace research questions about how immune recognition is studied in cancer and which measurements support the interpretation.
question: How do investigators connect antigen-presentation measurements with immune response without overstating causality?
approach: Locate primary experiments and inspect controls.
Distinguish expression measurements from functional assays.
Ask which observations reproduce in independent contexts.
cautions: Evidence from model systems may not translate directly to clinical outcomes.

title: Gene-expression data atlas
summary: Find expression datasets, assess metadata quality and design analyses that other researchers can repeat.
question: Which public datasets contain the measurements and patient-level labels needed for a transparent comparison?
approach: Record dataset accessions, source hashes and processing versions.
Distinguish raw counts, normalised expression and panel assays.
Plan tests and correction for multiple comparisons in advance.
cautions: Illustrated heatmaps are decorative. No patient measurements are visualised here.

title: Biomarker validation
summary: Assess whether a published biomarker claim can be independently checked, not simply repeated in the same dataset.
question: Was a proposed biomarker tested on truly independent data with compatible clinical endpoints?
approach: Check sample sizes, confidence intervals and data leakage risks.
Distinguish discovery from independent validation.
Report negative replications alongside positive results.
cautions: A significant association is not automatically a clinically useful or approved biomarker.

title: Clinical trial evidence
summary: Follow registered studies, endpoints and published outcomes while distinguishing study designs and evidence quality.
question: Which outcomes were prespecified, which were reported, and how were harms measured?
approach: Compare study registry entries and resulting publications.
Distinguish exploratory findings from prespecified endpoints.
Check eligibility criteria, follow-up time and limitations.
cautions: Clinical trial information is not patient-specific medical guidance.

sources.name: WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform

title: AI agents for evidence checking
summary: Design independent agents that retrieve source material, examine claims and submit structured critiques.
question: How can automated reviews identify missing citations, incompatible methods and unsupported conclusions?
approach: Require source URLs or persistent publication IDs.
Separate independent reviewers from the original authoring agent.
Treat all AI conclusions as suggestions until human scientific review.
cautions: Multiple agreeing models are not equivalent to scientific validation.

title: Reproducible open research
summary: Help contributors publish code, methods, sources, model versions and caveats together with their results.
question: Could a second team or independent agent repeat the result using the published methods and input data?
approach: Version all datasets, scripts and generated outputs.
Provide exact analysis settings and compute environment.
Log corrections and negative replication outcomes.
cautions: Public discussion and reproducibility records do not replace formal peer review.
